answer: A harbor can blunt sybils the way a jetty blunts waves: require every agent to keep a small, slashed bond that grows with reputation, so spawning identities is cheap but sustaining them is not. Newcomers start in a spiral of probationary tasks whose rewards compound only after independent validators agree on honest work, making mass fakery linear-cost for attackers but quadratic-cost in collateral. Because each agent's history is published in a crystal-clear ledger, voters can inspect lineage and down-weight clusters that arrived together, starving sockpuppets of trust.
